items.short_title: Prevent path collisions and incomplete output pairs

note_records.text: **2026-10-07** — Ready for review: branch ob-03-path-collisions, commit f25c523. Behaviour: obfuscate and deobfuscate reject any input/output/manifest pair that matches after Path.GetFullPath with a case-insensitive compare. Obfuscate stages the CSV and manifest as unique sibling .tmp files and publishes both only after both are written; on failure it deletes what it published and restores --force targets from .bak. A blank passphrase is now rejected before any work. ManifestCrypto.WriteManifest is replaced by WriteManifestTo (callers stage it). README overwrite paragraph updated. Checks: dotnet test Obfuscator.slnx 73/73 passed (8 new or extended tests failed before the change, including the gpg failure test, which ran); scripts/test-local.sh exit 0; slicer check passed. Follow-up: ob-12 (symlink and hard-link aliases).

**2026-10-07** — VERDICT: FAIL - Obfuscate_ManifestStageFailure_WithForce_PreservesBothExistingOutputs is now stopped by the early blank-passphrase check and never stages the manifest; manifest staging failure is covered only by the gpg test, which is skipped without gpg. Add a gpg-independent manifest staging failure test and rename the passphrase test.

**2026-10-07** — Ready for review (round 2): addresses FAIL verdict in b6e22d9. New Obfuscate_ManifestStageFailure_WithForce_PreservesExistingOutput (missing manifest dir, no gpg needed) fails on main (existing CSV overwritten) and passes on the branch; blank-passphrase test renamed to Obfuscate_BlankPassphrase_WithForce_PreservesBothExistingOutputs. dotnet test 74/74 passed; slicer check passed.

**2026-10-07** — Decisions (owner-approved 2026-10-07): Algorithm = AES-SIV-CMAC-256 (RFC 5297; two AES-128 keys), implemented in-repo in Obfuscator/AesSiv.cs on BCL Aes.EncryptEcb; a .NET 10.0.12 probe found no public CMAC/SIV type in the BCL. No new dependency. Token = OBF_TK2_ + base64url(SIV||CTR ciphertext) over UTF-8 + PKCS7 padding to 16 bytes (length leak unchanged from CBC). Per-column key = HKDF(master, '<column>|token-siv', 32); AD = column name. Joinability scope unchanged: per column, per manifest salt. Compatibility: manifest Version 2.1, ColumnObfuscationSpec.TokenScheme='aes-siv-cmac-256/v1' (omitted when null so 2.0 checksums verify); TokenScheme null => legacy OBF_TKN_ CBC decrypt-only path, CBC encrypt removed. Unknown scheme throws. Public API signatures unchanged.

**2026-10-07** — Ready for review: branch ob-04-aes-siv-tokens (c3c83a6 claim, 8bd80f3 implementation). Behaviour change: new deterministic tokens are AES-SIV OBF_TK2_; tampered or wrong-key tokens now throw InvalidOperationException without echoing values; old OBF_TKN_ manifests still deobfuscate. Checks: RFC 4493 CMAC vectors (4) and RFC 5297 A.1/A.2 pass; tamper/AD/truncation, equality/distinct/cross-column, prefix-leak regression, 15/16/17-byte + UTF-8 round-trip and length buckets, wrong key, legacy golden fixture (generated by main @ fc19ca7) pass; dotnet test Obfuscator.slnx 91/91 passed; scripts/test-local.sh exit 0, token columns restore exactly. macOS only locally; Linux/Windows left to CI. Round-trip tests are not a security argument: correctness rests on the RFC KATs and the construction still needs reviewer sign-off. Follow-up filed: ob-13 (float columns do not round-trip exactly; pre-existing).

**2026-10-08** — VERDICT: PASS. Reviewed AesSiv.cs line-by-line against RFC 4493 (subkeys, CMAC last-block handling) and RFC 5297 (S2V incl. xorend/pad branches, Q bit-31/63 clearing, 128-bit counter, constant-time tag compare, plaintext zeroed on failure); KATs RFC 4493 x4, RFC 5297 A.1/A.2 pass. Engine: per-column HKDF key with distinct info label, AD = column name, cache reset on each BindCrypto; no derivation collision with mapping mode (string mode is global per run). Compat: 2.0 manifests verify and decrypt via legacy path (golden fixture); older builds reject 2.1 token manifests via checksum mismatch rather than passing tokens through. Checks: dotnet test 91/91, scripts/test-local.sh exit 0, slicer check pass (macOS). Non-blocking: Version field is never validated on read; token AesSiv instances are not disposed after the final run.

items.short_title: Do not stage the manifest in shared temp before GPG encryption

note_records.text: **2026-10-08** — Ready for review: branch ob-17-gpg-stdin, commit 4c116de (slice promoted from the row on this branch). Behaviour change: ManifestCrypto.GpgEncryptTo pipes the payload to gpg stdin and reads ASCII armor from stdout; the obf-plain-*.tmp file in shared temp and the destPath.gpg side file are gone; RunGpg gained an optional stdin payload written after the stdout/stderr reads start. OBF_GPG_V2 format unchanged. Checks: new test Manifest_GpgEncrypt_WritesNoPlaintextToDiskWhileGpgRuns (POSIX gpg wrapper scans TMPDIR and output dir at invocation) logged 'found' before, 'clean' after, and round-trips; GPG tests 3/3; dotnet test Obfuscator.slnx 133/133; scripts/test-local.sh exit 0; slicer check passed. Residual: the stdin write is synchronous, so the 30 s gpg timeout only starts once gpg has taken the whole payload; --batch means gpg should not stall waiting on a prompt. No follow-ups filed.

fields.findings: Obfuscator/ManifestCrypto.cs:47-50 writes the pre-GPG manifest payload (plaintext JSON when no passphrase is set) to Path.GetTempPath() before gpg encrypts it, so an unencrypted copy briefly sits in the shared temp directory and survives a crash; stage it next to the destination or pipe it to gpg's stdin

Obfuscator.Cli/ObfuscatorCliProgram.cs ResolveDeterministicKey returns a whitespace-only env value, and Obfuscator/ObfuscationEngine.cs:34 treats it as no key, so auto string mode silently falls back to mapping; a blank --deterministic-key-file is rejected since ob-08

goals: Make CSV obfuscation and restoration safer to use for library and CLI users, while maintaining synthetic CSV generation as an equally important product capability. Harden the current 0.1 line over the next 1–2 releases, prioritizing safe data handling and risk reduction.
non_goals: Do not claim obfuscation alone provides cryptographic secrecy. Do not require encrypted manifests by default. Do not target a 1.0 release in this roadmap.
